title: Surface-Evaporation Call-Local Allocation and Scaling Qualification

scope_boundary.statement: F-PE11 addresses only call-local copying/allocation and throughput/scaling in the already-qualified restricted surface-evaporation runtime path. Existing scientific equations, constants, provider physics, supported-configuration scope and accepted observable semantics remain reference authority.

confirmed_owning_steps: kernel_committed_state_t%snapshot clones the private physical transaction state
fmr_build_committed_process_hydraulic_view allocates and copies pressure_head and water_content into soil_water_physical_state_t
build_process_hydraulic_view allocates and copies both profile arrays again
detached_state_from_view allocates and copies both profile arrays again before capacity evaluation

candidate.description: Retain the transactionally safe committed snapshot clone, then transfer the cloned allocatable profile arrays into a soil_water_physical_state_t with move_alloc. Route surface evaporation directly through that detached state. Do not alias committed state and do not change the surface-capacity provider contract.
candidate.expected_profile_copy_reduction: from committed clone plus three downstream full-profile copies to committed clone only in the surface-evaporation materialization path

non_goals: no change to restricted surface-evaporation equations or constants
no change to B110 surface-capacity equations or conductivity-mean policy
no widening of SWINTER/SWREDU or other qualified physical scope
no direct pointer/view into private committed physical state
no change to checkpoint, trial, commit or rollback semantics
no canonical promotion in this workunit
qualification_gates: compile at -O0 and -O2 with runtime checks
paired candidate-versus-F-CI41P observable identity using the frozen F-VQ56 surface-runtime oracles
detached ownership: mutating extracted temporary state cannot mutate committed state
committed state remains readable and identical after repeated extraction
no production changes outside the narrow runtime binding/materialization path
static allocation guard proving removed downstream allocate/copy sites do not reappear
paired timing characterization with identical workload and warm-up policy before any throughput claim
MultiSWAP scaling characterization before any scaling claim
